Further information: [Olympic Arts Festival](/wiki/Olympic_Arts_Festival "Olympic Arts Festival")

The original festivals in Olympia celebrated both cultural events and physical feats. The tradition continued with the first modern Olympics in 1896, and since then various cultural events have accompanied the sporting competition. Starting with the [1996 Summer Olympics](/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics"), a cycle of four arts festivals have been staged by each host country.[[35]](#cite_note-ciddor2001-38) The Sydney Olympic Arts Festival was an arts festival that ran before and during the Olympics.[[36]](#cite_note-39) The festival event coordinator was David Gallen.[[35]](#cite_note-ciddor2001-38)

The first of the four festivals was the first edition of the [Festival of the Dreaming](/wiki/Festival_of_the_Dreaming "Festival of the Dreaming"), which was founded by artistic director [Rhoda Roberts](/wiki/Rhoda_Roberts "Rhoda Roberts") (who later co-directed segments of the Opening Ceremony), was held in 1997, as the first of four leading up to the Sydney Olympics. Some events were held at the [Sydney Opera House](/wiki/Sydney_Opera_House "Sydney Opera House"), and the festival included an [Aboriginal](/wiki/Aboriginal_Australians "Aboriginal Australians") cast performing Shakespeare's *[A Midsummer Night's Dream](/wiki/A_Midsummer_Night%27s_Dream "A Midsummer Night's Dream")*, as well as [Samuel Beckett](/wiki/Samuel_Beckett "Samuel Beckett")'s *[Waiting for Godot](/wiki/Waiting_for_Godot "Waiting for Godot")* performed in the [Bundjalung language](/wiki/Bundjalung_language "Bundjalung language").[[37]](#cite_note-wired-40)[[35]](#cite_note-ciddor2001-38)

The second festival was "A Sea Change", in which artists and companies from Australia and [Oceania](/wiki/Oceania "Oceania") explored "the influence of the sea on Australian life as a means to explore the changing political and cultural climates in Australia".[[35]](#cite_note-ciddor2001-38)
